title: Founder case: Amazon starts with books

sources.claim: Amazon.com launched in July 1995 as an online bookstore, started from a rented house in Bellevue, Washington; Jeff Bezos chose books from a short list of products because of the huge number of titles in print and broad demand.

sections.skill: Apply a documented early decision: start online with one focused category

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Amazon.com sell when it launched?

choices.text: Groceries, clothing and electronics all at once

questions.intro: Documented history (HistoryLink, a Washington State history encyclopedia): Amazon.com launched in July 1995 as an online bookstore, started from a rented house in Bellevue, Washington. Jeff Bezos chose books from a short list of possible products because of the huge number of titles in print and broad demand. Lesson drawn by this course (an interpretation): start online with one focused category that suits the web's strengths, such as offering more choice than a physical store. One success story does not guarantee the same result for another business.

sections.skill: Why the web suited a huge catalog

questions.prompt: What limits a physical bookstore's selection?
questions.intro: A physical bookstore can hold only so many books on its shelves. A website is not limited by shelf space: it can list far more titles than any single store. That is one way to see why books fit the web well. The documented facts are the launch, the category and the reason given; the explanation of shelf space is this course's way of making the reason concrete.
